# `set_subframe`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set the camera crop (sub-frame) rectangle, in pixels.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xcf150, SetSubframe @0x11f4e0, VideoCapSetSubframe @0x20e2a0, SetCamSubframe @0x1553f0 (64-bit build) |

On the focus page this changes the in-memory video-capture rectangle; on other pages it calls the camera crop setter under the camera lock. Dimensions are multiplied by the bin factor, forced even, and clamped; sensor-axis swapping depends on a camera flag. If the SDK crop call fails the crop is cleared as a fallback, so read back with get_subframe rather than assuming the requested rectangle was applied.

Side effects: Changes the capture rectangle or camera crop; a crop failure can clear the crop.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_subframe"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array | yes | - | A crop rectangle object, or an array whose first element is that object. A positional [width, height, x, y] array is not accepted. `width` and `height` are required positive integers; `x` and `y` are optional signed integers (default -1, meaning centred; other JSON types are ignored). There is no upper bound in the handler; the helpers reject sizes exceeding the sensor (204). [READ] |

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | params absent or not an object (or array whose first element is not an object) | `expected object param` |
| 209 | width or height missing, not an integer, or not positive; also invalid dimensions in the helper | `invalid value` |
| 204 | Dimensions exceed the camera limits | `out of limit` |
| 210 | Unsupported model path in the helper | `not supported` |
| 318 | Camera absent, closed or SDK camera id unavailable | `device not connected` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Errors from the SDK crop call are not propagated directly (the clear fallback runs instead); fallback failures are unresolved. Model-specific sensor dimensions are not established.

## Example

Request, centred - Centred crop (values invented):

```json
{"id":70,"method":"set_subframe","params":{"width":1080,"height":1920}}
```

Request, offset - Explicit offset:

```json
{"id":71,"method":"set_subframe","params":{"width":800,"height":600,"x":100,"y":50}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_subframe","result":0,"code":0,"id":70}
```

Reply, bad-size:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_subframe","error":"invalid value","code":209,"id":72}
```
